cards.details: Drafted and moved by Jawaharlal Nehru in the Constituent Assembly, outlining the constitutional structure, values, and ideals. Unanimously adopted on January 22, 1947.
The Constituent Assembly adopted the Constitution including the Preamble. Note: The Preamble was enacted *after* the rest of the Constitution was already passed.
The Supreme Court ruled that the Preamble is a key to open the minds of the framers, but it is **NOT** a part of the Constitution. Therefore, it cannot be amended.

In this historic judgment, the Supreme Court reversed its previous stand, ruling that the Preamble **IS** a part of the Constitution and can be amended under Article 368, subject to the 'Basic Structure' doctrine.
Amended the Preamble for the first and only time. Added three words: **Socialist**, **Secular**, and **Integrity** (changing 'unity of the Nation' to 'unity and integrity of the Nation').
The Supreme Court once again held that the Preamble is an **integral part** of the Constitution of India.

mnemonics.title: Mnemonics & Memory Hacks
mnemonics.description: Use these simple memory hooks to remember the key sequences and components of the Preamble.

items.title: Mnemonic 1: Nature of the Indian State (Sequence)
items.decryption: Remember the exact order of description of India as a state: **S**overeign, **S**ocialist, **S**ecular, **D**emocratic, **R**epublic. (Tip: The three 'S' words are ordered by length: So-ve-reign [9], So-cia-list [9], Se-cu-lar [7] or alphabetically).

items.title: Mnemonic 2: Objectives of the Constitution
items.decryption:
Remember the four core values promised to all citizens:
- **J**ustice (Social, Economic, Political)
- **L**iberty (Thought, Expression, Belief, Faith, Worship)
- **E**quality (Status & Opportunity)
- **F**raternity (Dignity & Integrity)

items.title: Mnemonic 3: Words added by 42nd Amendment (1976)
items.decryption: The three words added to the Preamble by the 42nd Amendment: **S**ocialist, **I**ntegrity, **S**ecular. (Alternatively, remember **SSI**).

items.question: Is the Preamble justiciable or enforceable in a court of law?
items.answer: No. The Preamble is **non-justiciable**. Its provisions cannot be enforced in any court of law, and it is neither a source of power to the legislature nor a limitation on its powers.

items.question: Which country was the first to begin its Constitution with a Preamble?
items.answer: The **United States of America (USA)** was the first country to introduce a Preamble. The Indian Constitution followed this practice.

items.question: What is the source of authority of the Constitution as per the Preamble?
items.answer: The **People of India**. This is reflected in the opening phrase: 'We, the People of India...'.

items.question: Was the Preamble adopted before or after the enactment of the rest of the Constitution?
items.answer: It was enacted **after** the rest of the Constitution was already passed, to ensure that it was in complete alignment with all constitutional provisions.

items.question: Can the Preamble be amended to alter its basic features?
items.answer: No. While the Preamble is amendable under Article 368 (ruled in Kesavananda Bharati, 1973), its elements that form part of the **'Basic Structure'** cannot be amended or destroyed.

traps.title: UPSC Common Exam Traps to Avoid
items: Trap 1: Believing the Preamble is a source of legislative power or can restrict legislative action. The Supreme Court has explicitly clarified that it is non-justiciable and does not grant or strip legislative authority.

Trap 2: Confusing the types of Justice and Liberty. The Preamble promises **Social, Economic, and Political** Justice (not Religious or Cultural) and Liberty of **Thought, Expression, Belief, Faith, and Worship** (not Liberty of Action or Speech specifically, which are covered under Article 19).

Trap 3: Assuming that 'Socialism' in the Indian Preamble implies state control over all means of production. Indian Socialism is **Democratic Socialism** (a hybrid of public and private sectors, leaning towards a mixed economy), not Communistic Socialism (which involves nationalization of all property).
Trap 4: Assuming the Preamble has been amended multiple times. It has been amended **only once** so far, by the 42nd Amendment Act in 1976.

deepDive.title: Syllabus Core Study Notes (Deep-Dive)
deepDive.description: Explore the structural pillars, key terms, objectives, and legal boundaries of the Preamble to the Indian Constitution.

sections.title: 1. Ingredients and Keywords of the Preamble
sections.content:
The Preamble serves as the preface or introduction to the Constitution. Prominent jurist N.A. Palkhivala called it the 'Identity Card of the Constitution'. It contains four core ingredients:

Key Terms Explined:

  • Sovereign: India is completely independent and not a dominion of any external power. It is free to acquire foreign territory or cede a part of its own territory.
  • Socialist: Added by the 42nd Amendment (1976). India practices 'Democratic Socialism' (mixed economy) rather than 'Communistic Socialism' (state monopoly).
  • Secular: Added by the 42nd Amendment (1976). India embodies positive secularism—all religions have equal status, support, and protection from the State.
  • Democratic: Government by representation, based on universal adult franchise, periodic elections, rule of law, and independence of the judiciary.
  • Republic: The head of the state (President) is elected, not hereditary (unlike the British monarchy). Public offices are open to all citizens without discrimination.

sections.title: 2. Core Objectives: Justice, Liberty, Equality, Fraternity
sections.content:
The Preamble outlines the moral and socio-political objectives of the Constitution, which are detailed in the Fundamental Rights and Directive Principles.

Objective Dimensions promised Key Constitutional Linkages
Justice Social, Economic, and Political Secured through Fundamental Rights and DPSP (Article 38). Inspired by the **Russian Revolution (1917)**.
Liberty Thought, Expression, Belief, Faith, and Worship Secured through Fundamental Rights (Articles 19, 25-28). Inspired by the **French Revolution (1789)**.
Equality Status and Opportunity Secured through Articles 14-18 (Civic), Article 325 & 326 (Political), and Article 39 (Economic).
Fraternity Dignity of the individual; Unity & Integrity of the nation Promoted through single citizenship and Fundamental Duties (Article 51A). 'Integrity' was added in 1976.
The French Triad

The ideals of **Liberty, Equality, and Fraternity** in our Preamble were adopted from the French Revolution (1789-1799). Dr. B.R. Ambedkar stressed that these three values form a 'union of trinity' and cannot be divorced from one another; without equality, liberty would produce the supremacy of the few over the many.

sections.title: 3. Judicial Status and Amendability of the Preamble
sections.content:
The legal status of the Preamble evolved significantly through key Supreme Court judgments, settling whether it constitutes a part of the Constitution and its vulnerability to amendments under Article 368.

Case Supreme Court Ruling Significance & Rationale
Berubari Union Case (1960) Not a part of the Constitution The Court stated that while the Preamble shows the general purpose of the Constitution, it is not a part of it and cannot be used to override clear provisions.
Kesavananda Bharati Case (1973) Is a part of the Constitution Overruled the 1960 opinion. The Court noted that the Preamble was voted upon and passed by the Constituent Assembly just like the rest of the Constitution. Subject to Basic Structure.
LIC of India Case (1995) Integral part of the Constitution Reaffirmed that the Preamble is an intrinsic and integral component of the constitutional fabric.
Amendability under Article 368

In the **Kesavananda Bharati Case (1973)**, the Supreme Court ruled that because the Preamble is a part of the Constitution, it can be amended under Article 368. However, any amendment must respect the **Basic Structure Doctrine**.

The Preamble has been amended only once: the **42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976**, which added the words **Socialist, Secular, and Integrity**. The validity of this amendment has been upheld by the courts.

Two Key Rules on Preamble Status
  • Non-Justiciable: Its provisions cannot be enforced in a court of law. One cannot sue the government solely on the ground of violating the Preamble.
  • Neither Power nor Restriction: The Preamble is not a source of power for the legislature, nor does it act as a prohibition or limitation on legislative powers.
